thread:
Sam: quick heads-up — did a prompt-sensitivity sweep across quant levels for nova10b bring-up. short summary: int4 saves ~2.6-3x token cost but some prompts show non-trivial quality delta.
Maria: nice — can you paste the numbers? what slices did you test?
Sam: ran 6k eval prompts: mix of single-turn QA, code-gen, multi-turn chat snips. seq cap 1024. key aggregates below.
Sam: INT8 (fp16 baseline equivalent) — avg EM 86.4, mean MRR 0.872, failure tail (top-5 regressions) median drop 0.9%. cost ≈ $11.8 / 1M tokens
Sam: INT4 (dynamic quant) — avg EM 84.1, mean MRR 0.846, failure tail median drop 3.3%. cost ≈ $4.4 / 1M tokens
Priya: so ~2.3 point EM drop on average and some heavy tail regressions. how big are the regressions on critical slice?
Sam: on code-gen prompts with >200 tokens output EM-like correctness proxy drops 5-9% for int4. for short QA (<50 tokens) drop is ~0.5-1%.
Kevin: can you share the command/benchmark run?
Sam: sure — run command we used:
```
bench-eval --model nova10b --quant {int8,int4} --batch 1 --seq 1024 --prompts evalset_v2.csv --metrics em,mrr,latency
```
Sam: small sample rows (prompt_id,quant,em,mrr,lat(ms)):
```
12345,int8,1.0,1.0,210
12345,int4,0.0,0.0,195
54321,int8,0.8,0.84,220
54321,int4,0.75,0.78,200
```
Julia: latency roughly the same or slightly better with int4, so perf isn't the issue. this is purely quality delta.
Priya: product ask — what's the routing play? can we hybrid route based on prompt characteristics?
Sam: my proposal: default to int4 for low-risk routes (short QAs, embeddings, bulk summarization), route to int8 for: code-gen, long-context explained prompts (>512 tokens), and premium tier. fallback: if int4 output score (confidence proxy) < 0.7 then rerun on int8.
Kevin: what's the unit-econ impact of that hybrid? rough calc please.
Sam: rough back-of-envelope using our traffic mix (60% short Q/A, 25% summarization, 10% code-gen, 5% premium):
- All-int8 baseline cost: $11.8/1M tokens * 1 = $11.8
- All-int4 baseline cost: $4.4/1M tokens * 1 = $4.4
- Hybrid (int4 default + int8 for 15% of calls after signals): cost ≈ 0.85*$4.4 + 0.15*( $4.4 + extra rerun cost ) — net ~ $5.5/1M tokens (ballpark)
Sam: so ~53% cost reduction vs all-int8 while keeping most quality for high-risk slices.
Maria: what about the quality guardrails? need prompt-level signal that correlates with regression.
Sam: we tried two signals: 1) prompt length, 2) language token patterns (contains "```" or keywords like "implement", "optimize"). combined classifier (lightweight) recovers ~80% of the cases where int4 would fail significantly. precision about 0.78.
Julia: can we rely on confidence proxy from model output? any calibration drift with int4?
Sam: confidence proxy shifts a tad — we do a small recalibration per quant level (drop 0.03 on avg). after recalib threshold 0.7 works.
Priya: product note: for GTN/pilot customers we should offer "cost-saver" toggle with clear SLOs and an opt-out for codegen.
Kevin: ops note — we'll need rollout flags and metrics: per-route EM, rerun rate, extra latency P95. add canary with 5% traffic for 48h.
deploy-bot: Canary flag created: flag=ml.quant.hybrid.nova10b, bucket=5%, duration=48h
Sam: next actions: 1) instrument per-prompt signal and rerun counter (Sam), 2) add canary config and dashboards (Kevin), 3) product messaging + opt-outs (Priya), 4) finalize unit-econ doc and pricing knobs (Maria).
Priya: I'll draft the short product blurb: "Try cost-saver quant routing (int4 default) — estimated 2x cost reduction. Toggle off for codegen/premium." 
Maria: I'll own the unit-econ writeup and include sensitivity band for rerun rates (0-25%).
Kevin: I'll wire the observability: rerun_rate, int4->int8 fallback ratio, P95 latency delta, and per-slice EM.
Sam: happy to share full bench CSV and config in the eng-ml drive. ping me for access. :thumbsup:
Julia: thanks — this feels actionable. can we reconvene after 48h canary to decide expand/rollback?
Sam: yes — scheduled check-in in 2.5 days after canary ends.
Priya: tagging @product-leads for awareness.
